ashley: quick FYI — p99 for /v1/generate in the latency dashboard spiked ~40ms at 16:42 UTC but when i drill into endpoint-breakdown the per-endpoint p99s look flat. unsure if this is a rollup issue or sampling artifact :thinking_face:
miguel: which dashboard view? overall rollup or the new per-route snapshot view? link? :eyes: 
ashley: Observability > Latency > Endpoint breakdown (default 1h rollup). here's the snapshot time window: 16:40-16:45. looks like the global p99 (top-level) moved, but endpoints don't show it.
samir: can you paste the raw rollup query from the console or the tdigest output? might be a tdigest merge/precision thing.
ashley: pasted below (sanitized):
```
SELECT tdigest_percentile(merge(tdigest), 0.99) as p99
FROM latency_rollups
WHERE time >= '2026-03-19T16:40:00Z' AND time < '2026-03-19T16:45:00Z'
AND model = 'redwood-7b'
GROUP BY rollup_key
```
ashley: interestingly the rollup_key="global" shows p99=182ms but rollup_key for endpoint=/v1/generate shows p99=142ms.
elaine: could be routing-policy fallout: we recently started routing 10% of traffic to dedicated-region-b to test cheaper infra. if routing happened mid-window, merge semantics across tdigests with different shard skews can produce higher global p99 than any single endpoint bucket.
miguel: exact — tdigest isn't linear for tails. merging multiple tdigests from buckets with different quantile mass can create surprising higher percentiles. also depends on how we quantize sequences when building tdigest at ingestion.
samir: quick check: are endpoint-level rollups computed before or after route-weighted sampling? if we downsample differently per-route, merge will be weird.
ashley: endpoint rollups are from the per-node aggregator (pre-routing), global rollup is computed by downstream rollup job that merges per-node tdigest blobs. but we do a route-annotation later in the pipeline for the global view — possible mismatch.
elaine: created a quick grep in the logs:
```
2026-03-19T16:41:12Z aggregator[node-12]: emit tdigest sz=128 for /v1/generate
2026-03-19T16:41:13Z router: route assign=dedicated-region-b weight=0.1 req_id=...
2026-03-19T16:41:14Z rollup-job: merge tdigest shards global-window=2026-03-19T16:40
```
ashley: so routing changed mid-window -> per-endpoint aggregates might not include the small routed subset, but global does after route-annotation. that explains global > per-endpoint.
miguel: ok. mitigation idea: when we annotate routes we should keep route-keyed tdigest shards separate and only merge like-with-like, or update console to show aggregation method and merge mode (merge_all_shards vs weighted_merge).
samir: agree. UX ask: console should expose "aggregation algorithm" dropdown (tdigest-merge / sample-pctl / histogram-merge) and explain tradeoffs (accuracy vs cost). also add a tooltip: "percentile is computed from merged tdigests across shards — changes in routing during window may inflate tail."
elaine: filed ENG-2381 to: (1) add merge-mode toggle to dashboard, (2) change rollup job to produce per-route stable shards, (3) add a post-merge sanity check that flags global>max(endpoint) anomalies.
ashley: thanks. can we also add an alert for "global percentile > max(endpoint percentile)" for 2 consecutive windows — feels like a sign of merge/sampling mismatch.
miguel: +1. i'll prototype a quick check in the rollup job. samir want to own the console copy and CTA?
samir: i'll take console text + tooltip. will draft in product channel and loop in devex for wording.
ci-bot: build #rollup-job v2.14 started for commit abc123 — ETA ~3m :rocket:
ashley: will follow up with a small reproducible test: spin a routing canary and force differential sampling, collect raw histograms and tdigest dumps. posting results here once done. :white_check_mark:
